agent: mapdraw follow-up: the land border manager
question: What the land border lookup's extra (key, index) texels encode and how to compute them for a given state of who controls what: what fills CProvinceManager +0x42B4 and the border manager's +0x8C/+0x90/+0x9C, what 0x437980 does, who sets CBorderManager +0x59, and the formats of border_adj.bin and border_bitmap.bin.

addresses.name: CBorderManager_Construct
addresses.signature: CBorderManager* __stdcall CBorderManager_Construct(int tileHeight@ECX, int tileColumns@EDX, CBorderManager* borders@stack:4, CGraphics* graphics@stack:8, int tileWidth@stack:0xC, int tileRows@stack:0x10) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The CBorderManager constructor** (0xA0 bytes, operator new at VA 0x853B8B in CProvinceManager_CreateWorld, stored at WaterObject +0x415C). 0x434280 to the `ret 0x10` at 0x434839. Writes the vftable (rva 0x11E0F4C), +4 tile width (mgr +0x194), +8 tile height (+0x198, ECX), +0xC tile columns (+0x18C, EDX), +0x10 tile rows (+0x190), +0x14/+0x18 the powers of two at or above the map's width and height, +0x2C/+0x30 and +0x48/+0x4C the map's width W and height H (CMap +0x2A74/+0x2A78), +0x34 = float(tile width - 1), +0x38 g_CMap, +0x50 a W x H byte buffer, +0x54 the graphics object, +0x58 = graphics_settings +0x2C >= 0x200, **+0x40 = W + 1, +0x44 = H + 1** and **+0x3C = a (W+1) x (H+1) x 4-byte bitmap**. Then, where CMap cache_stale (+0x28) is 0 and `<dir>/cache/border_bitmap.bin` exists, the bitmap is read whole from it (0xA6C1B0 mode 0, 0xA6C880, 0xA6C7D0); otherwise two (W+1) x (H+1) byte masks are allocated at +0x60 and +0x64, CBorderManager_FillBitmap fills the bitmap, the file is written whole (mode 1, 0xA6D080) and the masks freed. Logs the time under 'CBorderManager::FillBitmap() <' (bordermanager.cpp). Last, +0x68 is resized to 60000 eight-byte elements (0x437AD0) and +0x78 to 90000 shorts (0x437B60); what either is for was not read. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x834280-0x834839 whole; one caller (findRefs --callers: VA 0x853BC2), whose pushes give the four stack arguments and whose ECX/EDX loads give the two register ones; retsBefore(0x834280, 0x83483C) is the one `ret 0x10`. The file size check: (5617 x 2161) x 4 = 48,553,348 bytes is exactly the install's tfh/map/cache/border_bitmap.bin. Would be wrong if the cached branch read the file in pieces or with a header - it is one read of +0x40 x +0x44 x 4 bytes into +0x3C.

addresses.name: CBorderManager_FillBitmap
addresses.comment: **Makes the border bitmap from the map**, only when border_bitmap.bin is missing or the map cache is stale (CBorderManager_Construct). 0x434910 to the `ret 4` at 0x4364A2. Reads the province raster (CMap +0x20E0, pixel (x, y) at +0x20 + x x +0xC + y x +0x18), each pixel's template (CMap +0x2A60[id]: +0x22 land, +0x7C id, +0x21 an unread byte) and **the first entry of CMapProvince +0x358's list** (the record's regions list), and the map.bin raster ([0x1A85578] +0xC, row stride +0x20 = W + 1). It never reads a controller. Byte 0 of each pixel = the province-border mask (+0x60, bits 1/2/4/8 for the x+1, x-1, y+1, y-1 neighbour, with the combination codes 3, 7, 11..15 and 19 at corners) ORed with the +0x64 mask, whose entries carry 0x10 where the two provinces' first +0x358 entries differ (so a region border, *inferred* from that field's name); byte 1 = 0x40, or 0xFF where three or more of the pixel and its four neighbours have no template, or less 10 per neighbour whose template +0x21 is set where a player country existed (in_game); **byte 2 is never written (0)**; byte 3 = a diagonal-cut code 1..6 where map.bin's low nibble marks a cut, +0x10 when the cut divides two different first +0x358 entries. The shipped file agrees: byte 2 is 0 in all 12,138,337 pixels, byte 0 takes 0..31 and byte 3 only 0..6 and 17..22. Only the outline above was read; the code that picks a corner code was read from the decompilation and not checked branch by branch. The name is from the log line its caller writes.
addresses.evidence: Headless decompilation of 0x834910 (DecompileAt, scratch copy of the project) checked against the listing for the extent (retsBefore gives the single ret 4 at 0x8364A2), the +0x358/+0x360 reads (0x834ADD-0x834AEC) and the absence of any +0x338 read inside 0x834910-0x8364A5. The byte histograms are from the shipped file. Inferred, not confirmed, because the corner-code ladder was taken from the decompilation; byte 0 and byte 3 do not need it for the rule (they are read from the file).

addresses.name: BorderManager_UpdateControllerBits
addresses.comment: **Writes each corner entry's country-border byte (byte 2) from the controllers.** 0x4365B0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4369D9; one caller, MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags (0x46111B), with that function's flags in EAX. For every corner entry, rows y in order and x ascending in each, that is **active** (+0x94 set) with x < +0x40 - 2 and y < +0x44 - 2: c, r, l, d, u = the templates (CMap +0x2A60[raster id]) at (x, y), (x+1, y), (x-1, y) where x-1 >= 1, (x, y+1), (x, y-1) where y-1 >= 1, else none. Where flags bit 1 is set, byte 1 = 0x14 first. Where three or more of the five are none: byte 1 = 0xFF if bit 1, **byte 2 left as it was**. Otherwise: if bit 1, byte 1 = 0x40, or where [0x170AD30] (Ghidra's g_FogOfWarEnabled) is set 0x28 when c is none or has +0x21 set, less 10 for each other one that is none or has +0x21 set; then, **if bit 0**: byte 2 = 0, and where c is a land template (+0x22) with an id (+0x7C), C = g_CMap +0x2200[c id] controller_id (+0x338), and for each neighbour n that is a land template with an id whose controller differs from C and whose map.bin byte m is clear of a mask: **byte 2 |= 1 for x+1 (m(x+1, y) & 0x0E == 0), 2 for x-1 (m(x-1, y) & 0x0B == 0), 4 for y+1 (m(x, y+1) & 0x0A == 0), 8 for y-1 (m(x, y-1) & 0x0F == 0)**. The lookup never reads byte 1. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x8365B0-0x8369D9), every branch: the flag split at 0x8365B6-0x8365CA, the bounds at 0x836623/0x836634, the five raster reads, the none count at 0x83679D-0x8367C6, the four controller compares at 0x8368AB/0x836901/0x83694B/0x836994 and the four map.bin masks at 0x8368C5/0x836912/0x83695F/0x8369A6. The caller loads EAX from its own first argument at 0x861117. Would be wrong if the template array were indexed by something other than the raster id - 0x836658-0x83666A builds it from the two raster bytes.

addresses.name: BorderManager_ApplyDiagonalCuts
addresses.comment: **The diagonal pass over the corner entries**, run after BorderManager_UpdateControllerBits when flags bit 0 is set. 0x4369E0 to the `ret 4` at 0x436BA7. Over the active entries with x < +0x40 - 2 and y < +0x44 - 2, in order, with L, R = the entries at x-1, x+1 of the same row (the neighbours in the array) and Y-, Y+ = the entries at (x, y-1) and (x, y+1) through the +0x98 pair: where byte 2 is 0, byte 3 &= ~8 (when byte 3 is not 0); else where byte 3 != 0 and m = map.bin(x, y) has a low nibble, four tests in order on byte 2 as it stands: (b2 & 5) and (m & 1): byte 3 |= 8, clear b2 bit 4 unless Y+.b2 & 8, clear bit 1 unless R.b2 & 2; (b2 & 0xA) and (m & 2): byte 3 |= 8, clear bit 8 unless Y-.b2 & 4, clear bit 2 unless L.b2 & 1; (b2 & 9) and (m & 8): byte 3 |= 8, clear 8 unless Y-.b2 & 4, clear 1 unless R.b2 & 2; (b2 & 6) and (m & 4): byte 3 |= 8, clear 4 unless Y+.b2 & 8, clear 2 unless L.b2 & 1. **Nothing clears byte 3 bit 3 where byte 2 is non-zero and no test fires**, so the bit can survive from an earlier refresh. The +0x98 cursor advances only on entries that pass the bounds, while BuildCornerCache gave a pair to every active entry; in TFH the only active entries out of bounds are the 57 in row H - 1, the last row, so nothing after them is misread. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x8369E0-0x836BB3, including the b2 == 0 tail at 0x836BAA). The +0x98 offsets: the first of a pair is added to the entry index and gives the row above (y-1), as BuildCornerCache builds it from the row range +0x8C[y-1]. The 57 is counted from border_adj.bin (pairs with y = 2159; none with x >= 5615).

addresses.name: BorderManager_SpreadCornerBits
addresses.comment: **The last corner pass**, after BorderManager_ApplyDiagonalCuts. 0x436BC0 to the `ret 4` at 0x436D53. Over the active entries in bounds, in order, t = byte 3 & 7: **t = 1 or 2** - copy byte 2's bits to the neighbours' byte 2, mirrored: b2 & 2 sets L.b2 |= 1, b2 & 1 sets R.b2 |= 2, b2 & 4 sets Y+.b2 |= 8, b2 & 8 sets Y-.b2 |= 4; **t = 3**: byte 3 bit 3 set where L.b3 == 9 or Y+.b3 == 9, else cleared; **t = 4**: L.b3 == 10 or Y-.b3 == 10; **t = 5**: R.b3 == 9 or Y-.b3 == 9; **t = 6**: R.b3 == 10 or Y+.b3 == 10; t = 0 or 7: nothing. The comparisons are on the whole byte, so a code carrying the 0x10 flag (0x19, 0x1A) never matches. The neighbours it writes may be inactive entries, which BorderManager_UpdateControllerBits never resets, so their byte 2 keeps what was ORed in. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x836BC0-0x836D53): the type switch at 0x836C5A-0x836CD6 with the byte compares at 0x836C81-0x836CDF, and the four ORs at 0x836D02-0x836D2D. EBX holds the first +0x98 offset (y-1) and EDI the second (y+1).

addresses.name: CBorderManager::BuildCornerCache
addresses.comment: **Builds the sparse 'corner cache' the lookup reads, and frees the bitmap.** 0x436D60 to the `ret 4` at 0x43749C; one caller, CProvinceManager_CreateMeshes (0x458768, logged 'Used RAM (corner cache)'), with &WaterObject +0x42B4, only while +0x88 is 0. For every province's list of (x, y) pairs: the entry for (x, y) in row y's scratch vector gets the bitmap's four bytes at (x, y) and a flag of 1 (added if absent, overwritten if there); then each of (x+1, y) where x+1 < +0x40, (x, y+1) where y+1 < +0x44, (x-1, y) where x >= 1 and (x, y-1) where y >= 1 is added with its own bitmap bytes and a flag of 0 **if absent** (CornerVector_PushBack, 12-byte {x, bytes, flag}). Each row is sorted by x (0x437F70). Then flattened: **+0x8C** an int array of +0x44 + 1 row starts, **+0x90** the x of each entry (int16), **+0x94** active = the flag and 1 <= y < +0x44 - 1, **+0x9C** the four bytes, **+0x98** two int16 per active entry - the index of the same x in row y-1, then in row y+1, each minus the entry's own index (-1 minus it where absent). Last, the bitmap (+0x3C) and +0x50 are freed and **+0x88 = 1**. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of the head (0x836D60-0x836F3D: the bitmap read at 0x836DD8, the flag 1 push at 0x836E4A / overwrite at 0x836E7A, the flag 0 neighbour push at 0x836EFB) and the decompilation of the rest checked against the stores at 0x837182 (+0x8C) and 0x8371CD (+0x9C). The one caller and its +0x88 gate are at 0x85874F-0x858768. Would be wrong if the neighbours took the centre's bytes - 0x836E8F-0x836EB8 reads the bitmap at (x+1, y).

addresses.name: CBorderManager::OnResetDevice
addresses.comment: **CBorderManager's CLostDeviceInterface slot 1, and the only setter of the dirty byte.** 0x437950 to the bare `ret` at 0x437970: dirty (+0x59) = 1, rebuild_countdown (+0x5C) = 2, then BorderManager_Tick(this, [0x1A855FC] +0x5F2C) - which counts to 1 and returns, so the next frame's tick from MapGraphics_Update rebuilds the lookup texture. The lookup lives in D3DPOOL_DEFAULT (CViewsTextureManager::CreateTextures), so a device reset loses it and this refills it two frames later. Slot 0 is the shared empty stub 0xABF890. It opens `mov eax, [abs]` (0xA1), outside functionStart's prologue set, which is why fieldchain.py attributes its store to 0x4374D0 (trap 2). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: vtable.py --holding 0x837950: CBorderManager slot 1 only (table VA 0x15E0F4C, whose slot 0 is 0xABF890). Body read whole. Only setter: a scan for stores to [reg+0x59] (fieldchain --field 0x59 --writes) finds this one and the tick's clear in the map code; the holder scan [[x+0x415C]+0x59] finds no reader at all while its positive control [[x+0x415C]+0x88] finds CreateMeshes's read - so the negative is only that no other code reaches +0x59 through the graphics pointer.

addresses.name: DequeRect_PushBack
addresses.signature: void __stdcall DequeRect_PushBack(void* deque@ESI, const int* rect@stack:4)
addresses.comment: **std::deque push_back of a 16-byte rectangle** (x, y, width, height), growing the map through 0x437BF0 ('deque<T> too long'). 0x437980 to the `ret 4` at 0x4379EA. **It is not a bitmap fill**: BorderManager_Tick pushes (1, 1, +0x40 - 2, +0x44 - 2) onto a deque on its stack and destroys the deque (Deque_Tidy) without reading it; MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags pushes each changed province's padded box, or the whole map. Four callers. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: size/offset/map at deque +4/+8/+0xC/+0x10, a 0x10-byte block allocated per slot, two movq copies of the rectangle. The grow helper's string is at 0x837C11. Callers from findRefs --callers.

addresses.name: CornerVector_PushBack
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CornerVector_PushBack(const void* item@EAX, void* vector@EDI)
addresses.comment: push_back of a 12-byte {int x, uint8_t bytes[4], uint8_t flag} onto a std::vector (begin +0, end +4, capacity +8), with the usual aliasing branch when the item lies inside the vector. 0x437A50 to bare `ret`s at 0x437AA2 and 0x437ACB. Used by CBorderManager::BuildCornerCache.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing; the 12-byte stride is the 0x2AAAAAAB divide and the three copies (dword, dword, byte).

addresses.name: Deque_Tidy
addresses.comment: std::deque's clear-and-free: pops every element (size +0x10 to 0, offset +0xC to 0), frees each block of the map (+4, +8 entries) and the map, and zeroes +4 and +8. Element-size free, so shared by every deque instantiation; 45 callers. 0x4E7DD0 to the bare `ret` at 0x4E7E33.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing. Class-free on purpose: findRefs --callers gives 45 direct callers across the image.

addresses.name: BorderAdjCache_Write
addresses.comment: **Writes `<dir>/cache/border_adj.bin`** from WaterObject +0x42B4: int32 count of lists (the vector's 16-byte elements), then for each an int32 n and n x 8 bytes. 0x474310 to the `ret 4` at 0x4745F8. Called by CProvinceManager_CreateMeshes (0x458549) where the cache is stale or BorderAdjCache_Read failed. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation checked against the listing for the three writes (0xA6D080) and the >> 4 / >> 3 element counts; the format parses the install's 345,888-byte file exactly (14,169 lists, 36,151 pairs).

addresses.name: BorderAdjCache_Read
addresses.comment: **Reads `<dir>/cache/border_adj.bin` into WaterObject +0x42B4**: int32 count (false where <= 0 or the file is missing), the vector resized to it, then each list's int32 n and n x 8 bytes. **Each 8-byte element is (int32 x, int32 y)**, a pixel of the map in the engine's coordinates (y from the south), one per junction quad of the province's border mesh. 0x474600 to a `ret 4` at 0x4747AE with a cold block after it (0x4747B1, trap 3). Called by CProvinceManager_CreateMeshes (0x45853F) where the map cache is not stale. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation checked against the listing for the reads (0xA6C880). Measured: x runs 612..5518 and y 79..2159 in the file; every one of the 36,151 pairs is a pixel of its own province in provinces.bmp (file row 2159 - y) with 3 or 4 distinct ids among it and its four neighbours; and every one of the 151,408 cache border vertices whose lookup slot is past the province's adjacency count (adjacencies.bin) sits on the corner of pair (slot - count)'s pixel, all within the list.

addresses.name: MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags
addresses.signature: void __stdcall MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags(WaterObject* mgr@EDI, uint32_t flags@stack:4, void* changedProvinces@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **The map renderer's refresh by flags**, called by CInGameIdler_RefreshMap (0x25190E, with the idler's +0x84 and +0x88) and CFrontEnd::Update (0x2EE102). 0x460D30 to the `ret 8` at 0x461472, a cold block after it. Builds a deque of dirty rectangles (DequeRect_PushBack): the whole map inside a one-pixel margin when the changed-province list is empty, holds -1 or has more than 100 entries, else each province's bounding box (template +0x80..+0x8C) padded by 2. **Flags bit 0**: BorderManager_UpdateControllerBits(flags, borders), BorderManager_ApplyDiagonalCuts, BorderManager_SpreadCornerBits, then ViewsTextureManager_UpdateBorderLookup - over every corner entry, not only the rectangles. Bit 2, where +0x42E8 is set: the tree slots (+0x134) of tiles meeting the rectangle are freed, or all of them and MapObjects_RebuildTileStrips. Bit 1: each province entry's template +0xA8 = Province_IsHiddenByFog. Then, where CMap +0x2A8C is set, +0x44 = 1 on every object of each tile's +0x120 list. Province_SetController sets bit 0 of the idler's flags (VA 0x4A3585) when the controller really changed, and pushes the province id onto +0x88 (-1 past 110 entries). Only the border block was read closely. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, section B.7.
addresses.evidence: Border block read on the listing (0x86110D-0x861144, EAX = the flags at 0x861117); the rest from the decompilation. retsBefore gives the one ret 8. The SetController write: a byte scan for `or [reg+0x84], imm` over .text finds `or dword ptr [eax+0x84], 1` at VA 0x4A3585, after `cmp esi, [ebx+0x338]; je` - the controller test. Inferred because bits 1 and 2 and the tile loop were not checked branch by branch.

addresses.name: BorderManager_Tick
addresses.comment: Called every frame by MapGraphics_Update (at 0x45D616) with the border manager (graphics +0x415C) in EDI, and once by CBorderManager::OnResetDevice: where its dirty byte (+0x59) is set, counts +0x5C down, and at 0 **rebuilds the lookup texture** (ViewsTextureManager_UpdateBorderLookup) from the corner entries as they stand and clears the dirty byte. It changes no corner entry. **Corrected 2026-11-06**: this said it 'refills its bitmap over (1, 1) - (width-2, height-2) with 0x437980'; 0x437980 is a deque push_back (DequeRect_PushBack) of that rectangle onto a deque on the tick's stack, which Deque_Tidy destroys unread - and the bitmap (+0x3C) no longer exists by then, BuildCornerCache having freed it. The only setter of +0x59 is CBorderManager::OnResetDevice (device reset). 0x4364B0 to the `ret 4` at 0x43657E. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, sections B.3 and B.7.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x8364B0-0x8365AA): the deque is built at [esp+0x28] (proxy operator new(8), map/size zeroed), ESI = the deque at the push_back call 0x83654B, then 0x8826C0, the clear at 0x836559, Deque_Tidy (0x8E7DD0, ESI still the deque) and the proxy freed. Nothing between the push and the tidy reads the deque.

addresses.name: ViewsTextureManager_UpdateBorderLookup
addresses.comment: **Fills the 512x512 land border lookup texture** (textures +0x14, TerrainShader_Border's tex4, BorderDirectionTexture), D3DLOCK_DISCARD, written as one linear run of texels from the locked base (the pitch is not used; 512 x 4 bytes, so rows run on). Province i (from 1, over the province entries) is written from texel 14i: first one per adjacency entry of its template (+0x90/+0x94, 0x14 bytes each, the neighbour id at +4; the same count as adjacencies.bin's record), **0x000000FF where the neighbour's controller (CMapProvince +0x338) is the province's own and 0x400000FF where it is not** - B = 1.0 either way, A = 0.25 marking a change of controller; **then one per (x, y) pair of WaterObject +0x42B4[i]** (border_adj.bin): the corner entry for pixel (x, y), found by a linear search of row y (border manager +0x8C[y]..+0x8C[y+1]) of +0x90 for x - with no not-found arm, the pointer would be null - written as **A = byte0 x 8, R = byte2 x 8, G = byte3 x 8, B = 0** of that entry's four bytes (+0x9C) - the province pattern column, the country column (controllers, BorderManager_UpdateControllerBits) and the diagonal column. Before each province, the texels from where the last one stopped up to 14i are zeroed. **There is no cap at 14**: 162 TFH provinces have more than 14 adjacencies and pairs together, their tail runs into the next province's texels and is overwritten by it, which is where about 550 cache vertices of theirs look. Callers: BorderManager_Tick and MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags (flag bit 0). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, sections B.3 and B.7.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x8826C0-0x882971); key/index are x/y by the measurement under BorderAdjCache_Read. The 162 and ~550: adjacencies.bin counts plus border_adj.bin list lengths, and 553 cache vertices whose texel minus 14 x colour id is a pair slot at or past 14 (529 of them on that pair's pixel). The no-cap reading is the reset of EDI to 14i at 0x882820 with no bound on the two inner loops.

struct_fields.name: tile_width
struct_fields.comment: The map tile width (WaterObject +0x194, 50); +0x34 holds it less 1 as a float.
struct_fields.evidence: CBorderManager_Construct stores its stack argument 3 here (0x8342A5); the caller pushes WaterObject +0x194 (0x853BA9).

struct_fields.name: tile_height
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from ECX at 0x8342B4; the caller loads ECX from WaterObject +0x198 at 0x853BBB.

struct_fields.name: tile_columns
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from EDX at 0x8342B7; the caller loads EDX from +0x18C at 0x853BB4.

struct_fields.name: tile_rows
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from stack argument 4 at 0x8342BA; the caller pushes +0x190 first (0x853BAF).

struct_fields.name: map_width
struct_fields.comment: The map's width W (CMap +0x2A74); +0x48 holds it again.

struct_fields.name: map_height
struct_fields.comment: The map's height H (CMap +0x2A78); +0x4C holds it again.

struct_fields.name: map
struct_fields.comment: g_CMap: the province raster (+0x20E0), templates (+0x2A60) and provinces (+0x2200) the corner passes read.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from [0x1A8557C] at 0x8342D6; read as the CMap by the passes (0x83663A, 0x836882).

struct_fields.name: bitmap
struct_fields.comment: The border bitmap, (W+1) x (H+1) pixels of four bytes, row y at y x +0x40 x 4: read whole from cache/border_bitmap.bin or made by CBorderManager_FillBitmap. Byte 0 the province pattern column, 1 a shade the lookup ignores, 2 the country column (0 in the file), 3 the diagonal code. **Freed by CBorderManager::BuildCornerCache**, which keeps only the corner pixels (+0x9C), so it does not exist in a running game; QuadBuild_EdgeVertices reads bytes 0 and 3 on the rebuild path before that.
struct_fields.evidence: Allocated (W+1)(H+1) x 4 at 0x8344E7-0x83450E, read from the file at 0x834578, freed by BuildCornerCache at 0x83742D-0x837436 (free, then +0x3C = 0; +0x50 the same at 0x837439-0x837445, +0x88 = 1 at 0x837448). The file's size matches.

struct_fields.name: graphics
struct_fields.comment: The graphics object; its graphics_settings (+0x6BC48) +0x2C >= 0x200 gives the byte at +0x58.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from stack argument 2 at 0x8342FF; the caller pushes WaterObject +0x3C (0x853BB0), the CGraphics.

struct_fields.name: dirty
struct_fields.comment: Set: BorderManager_Tick counts rebuild_countdown down and at 0 rebuilds the lookup texture from the corner entries, then clears it. **Set only by CBorderManager::OnResetDevice** (with the countdown at 2), so a device reset refills the lookup; a change of controller goes through MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags instead and never touches this.
struct_fields.evidence: OnResetDevice's store at 0x837956; fieldchain --field 0x59 --writes over the map code finds it and the tick's clear (0x836559) and nothing else.

struct_fields.name: fill_province_mask
struct_fields.comment: Scratch (W+1) x (H+1) bytes for CBorderManager_FillBitmap: the province-border bits, ORed into byte 0 at the end. Freed by the constructor after the fill.
struct_fields.evidence: Allocated and zeroed at 0x834596-0x8345C9, freed at 0x834634-0x834638; written throughout 0x834910.

struct_fields.name: fill_region_mask
struct_fields.comment: Scratch (W+1) x (H+1) bytes for CBorderManager_FillBitmap: border bits carrying 0x10 where the two sides' first CMapProvince +0x358 entries differ, ORed into byte 0. Freed by the constructor.
struct_fields.evidence: Allocated at 0x8345B1, freed at 0x83463D-0x834644; the 0x10/0x11..0x18 writes in 0x834910.

struct_fields.name: corner_cache_built
struct_fields.comment: Set by CBorderManager::BuildCornerCache; CProvinceManager_CreateMeshes builds the cache only while it is 0.
struct_fields.evidence: Cleared by the constructor (0x834317), set at the end of 0x836D60, tested at 0x858755.

struct_fields.name: corner_row_starts
struct_fields.comment: +0x44 + 1 ints: row y's corner entries are indices [corner_row_starts[y], corner_row_starts[y+1]) of +0x90/+0x94/+0x9C.
struct_fields.evidence: Allocated (+0x44 + 1) x 4 and filled by BuildCornerCache (0x837182); read by the lookup (0x88289D) and the three passes as a row range.

struct_fields.name: corner_x
struct_fields.comment: Each corner entry's x, ascending within a row.
struct_fields.evidence: Written by BuildCornerCache after the per-row sort; the lookup's search assumes ascending order (jle at 0x8828C6).

struct_fields.name: corner_active
struct_fields.comment: 1 for a corner entry that came from a border_adj.bin pair and lies in rows 1..+0x44 - 2; 0 for the neighbours added around it. Only active entries are rewritten by the passes.
struct_fields.evidence: BuildCornerCache's flag test against the row bounds; tested first in each pass (0x836606, 0x836A26, 0x836C06).

struct_fields.name: corner_vertical_links
struct_fields.comment: Two int16 per active entry, in entry order: the index of the same x in row y-1, then in row y+1, each minus the entry's index (-1 minus it where absent).
struct_fields.evidence: Built at the end of BuildCornerCache; read as ESI/EDX (0x836A6C) and EBX/EDI (0x836C3C) in the passes.

struct_fields.name: corner_values
struct_fields.comment: Each corner entry's four bitmap bytes, as kept and then rewritten: byte 0 the province column, byte 1 a shade the lookup ignores, byte 2 the country column (BorderManager_UpdateControllerBits, SpreadCornerBits), byte 3 the diagonal code with bit 3 for a country cut. The lookup writes A = byte0 x 8, R = byte2 x 8, G = byte3 x 8.
struct_fields.evidence: Allocated 4 per entry and filled from the bitmap by BuildCornerCache (0x8371CD); the passes' byte offsets +1/+2/+3; the lookup's read at 0x882966.

struct_fields.name: border_lookup_extras
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a per-province vector (16-byte elements, sized from border_adj.bin's count; end at +0x42B8) of std::vectors of 8-byte **(int32 x, int32 y) map pixels** - one per junction quad of the province's border mesh, each a pixel of the province where three or four provinces meet. Read from cache/border_adj.bin (BorderAdjCache_Read), written back by BorderAdjCache_Write, filled on the rebuild path by QuadBuild_EdgeVertices. ViewsTextureManager_UpdateBorderLookup turns pair k into the texel after the province's adjacency texels; CBorderManager::BuildCornerCache makes the corner entries from them.
struct_fields.evidence: The load/save formats and the measurements recorded under BorderAdjCache_Read.
